title: Man Returned From Mexico, Jailed on Capital Murder Charge in Laredo’s Fifth Homicide of 2026
excerpt: Christian Onyx Benson, 21, was picked up in Monterrey and brought back across International Bridge 1 to face a capital murder charge in the July death of Dora Alicia Peña, 56.
content:
A 21-year-old man accused of killing a Laredo woman in July has been returned from Mexico and jailed on a capital murder charge, Laredo police said Friday, Nov. 20.

Christian Onyx Benson was picked up Thursday evening in Monterrey, Nuevo León, and the Laredo Police Department learned of the arrest around 6:25 p.m., according to KGNS. Investigators coordinated with Mexican officials and a U.S. Marshals Service task force to bring him back. Task force officers received him at International Bridge 1 and drove him to police headquarters. Jail records list him as booked Friday in the Webb County Jail, with bond set at $1 million.

The charge stems from the death of Dora Alicia Peña, 56. A call about an unresponsive person brought officers to 113 Broadcrest Drive at about 8:22 a.m. on July 20, and Peña was pronounced dead there. Police said the death first appeared to be natural, but a medical examiner’s autopsy then turned up signs of foul play, and detectives from the Crimes Against Persons Unit interviewed several people of interest, including Benson.

According to police, Benson knew Peña and her relatives and was close to her son. Investigators concluded he went inside the residence and caused her death. Police Chief Miguel Rodriguez said Benson sexually assaulted Peña and that she died of suffocation, and that evidence also indicated a blow. The chief said Benson acknowledged to detectives that he was responsible for her death.

Police described Peña’s death as the fifth homicide recorded in Laredo this year. Benson is presumed innocent unless convicted in court.

Update — November 23, 2026: Dora Alicia Peña's son, Eleazar Peña, spoke publicly for the first time since the arrest, saying his family is waiting to face Benson in court. Peña, 56, was a widow who did everything for her children, her son said. Police Chief Miguel Rodriguez described Benson as “a friend” of Peña; Eleazar Peña said his brother met Benson at a nightclub and that Benson occasionally came to the family home for a beer or something to eat. Eleazar Peña said he distrusted Benson and warned his mother and brother. “It looked like a long way, but they got him. They, they did their job. We're grateful,” he said. The district attorney's office said Benson has not been indicted and no court date has been set, and that the arrest affidavit was not yet available in the system.

Source: KGNS; Laredo Police Department.
